target_customer: Indian startups and SMEs needing corporate cards, vendor payments, and forex remittances
problem: Indian startups could not get corporate credit cards without personal guarantees or collateral, and lacked spend management and working capital tools.
business_model: Card interchange, vendor payment and forex fees, plus interest on credit with bank and lender partners
product_category: Corporate cards and spend management fintech

founders.name: Pei-fu Hsieh
previous_startups: Incubated close to ten fintech companies in Indonesia, India and Brazil (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists only this founder.

founders.name: Amit Jangir
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in Inc42, Feb 2022.

founders.name: Kartik Jain
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in Inc42, Feb 2022.

founders.name: Sunil Sinha
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in Inc42, Feb 2022.

competitors.name: Happay
competitors.what: Expense management and corporate cards for Indian enterprises

competitors.name: Kodo
competitors.what: YC-backed spend management and corporate cards in India

technical_complexity.rationale: Card program management through bank partners (SBM Bank, M2P) plus credit underwriting; mostly integration and risk work, not novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Depends on bank partnerships and underwriting data; rivals such as Happay, RazorpayX and Kodo offered similar products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: RazorpayX launched a founder friendly corporate card later; Karbon remained independent through 2025.

market_need_then: India's startup boom with few corporate cards for young companies; one 2025 analysis estimates about 5 percent card penetration among 63 million MSMEs. Inc42 reports 2,000 corporates served and $30M monthly GTV in December 2021.

rebrands.to: Karbon Business (product line naming seen in 2025 launches)

brand_strength.rationale: Brand name collides with Karbon HQ and Carbon (Nigeria); no source on brand impact.

outcome_analysis: Karbon raised seed money in 2020, a $12M pre-Series A in September 2021 and a $15M Series A in February 2022, then took debt for lending. It reports serving 3,000 companies and kept launching products through 2025, with no exit or shutdown found, so it is an active growth stage company in a competitive Indian card market.
notes: The $2M seed (Inc42) and the $1M angel round (YourStory, April 2020) may overlap; one summary says the $1M was separate and added to a seed round, so counts could double. Total equity about $32M per Inc42, CB Insights lists $38.3M over 8 rounds including debt. Debt amount shown as INR 55 crore; USD not recorded. Competitor entries come from a February 2022 article, about six months after the Summer 2021 batch. Karbon website fetch returned 503. Series B not found.
